schema_note: One window only, the plan's own. trip-windows/1 (overview spec 2.2) needs 2 to 4 windows, so this file keeps the same field names under trip-season-basic/1 and adds a `season` block in the adapter's Season shape.
months_basis_note: The plan's own months: a two-day stopover over the turn of September into October.

sources.title: U.S. Climate Normals 1991-2020, monthly, LINCOLN NEPP, NH (USC00274734)
sources.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

points.name: Lincoln NEPP climate station
points.note: Station coordinates from the NCEI station record; Lincoln sits at the west end of the Kancamagus Highway, south of Franconia Notch.

label.value: Two days at the turn of September and October

why.value: The plan's own two days on the way to Vermont; normals at Lincoln give cool days and nights falling toward freezing.

tempC.value: 8 to 22 C in September, 2 to 14 C in October (mean daily low to high, Lincoln)
tempC.note: 1991-2020 normals: Sep max 22.0, min 8.3; Oct max 14.2, min 2.1. The station is in the valley at Lincoln; no 1991-2020 normals station in Franconia Notch or on the Kancamagus was found, so the higher stops are not covered by these values.

rain.value: About 97 mm in September and 138 mm in October
rain.note: The count of days with 1 mm or more (MLY-PRCP-AVGNDS-GE010HI) is not published for this station; asked for it in the request, none returned.

daylight.value: Sunrise about 06:40, sunset about 18:30; just under 12 hours of day
daylight.note: core/bin/sun.ts at the station point for both plan days: sunrise 06:42 to 06:43, sunset 18:32 to 18:30, day 11h50m to 11h47m.

notes.text: October is the wettest of the two months at Lincoln

windows.label: Two days at the turn of September and October
windows.verdict_note: Not set: only the plan's own window was researched, so there is nothing to rank it against.
windows.best_for: A morning in the notch and on the highway on the way to Vermont

minus.text: Cold early mornings, near 2 to 8 C in the valley at Lincoln
